newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss chemical exports rise 10.2 pct in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Swiss chemical exports rise 10.2 pct in H1 1997.

text.p: Swiss chemical exports rose 10.2 percent to 14.6 billion Swiss francs in the first half of 1997, while imports rose 19.0 percent to 8.1 billion, the Swiss Society of Chemical Industries said.
Imports from the European Union (EU), which account for 83 percent of all chemical imports, rose 14.6 percent in the first half, up from 4.1 percent last year, the society said in a statement.
Exports to the EU rose 12.0 percent, well up from the 3.2 percent growth rate in the first half of 1996.

Exports to Germany, the largest recipient of Swiss chemical exports, rose 17.2 percent to 2.67 billion francs from 1.7 percent last year, while exports to France, the second largest recipient, rose 3.7 percent, against a 2.8 percent decline.
Exports to the United States rose 12.3 percent, down from 18.5 percent last year, while exports to Latin America surged 17.6 percent, up from a 4.3 percent rise last year.
Helped by an 11.5 percent rise in exports to Japan, up from 1.2 percent last year, exports to Asia rose 8.2 percent, up from a 1.6 percent rise last year.
